summary.short: Replaces Council Directive 85/374/EEC with EU rules on no-fault liability for defective products, including software, for manufacturers and other economic operators. Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 9 December 2026; Member States must transpose by that date.
summary.long: Replaces Council Directive 85/374/EEC with EU rules on no-fault liability for damage caused by defective products. 'Product' includes software, electricity, digital manufacturing files and raw materials (Art. 4(1)). Liable are manufacturers, manufacturers of defective components, importers, authorised representatives and fulfilment service providers (for non-EU manufacturers), and conditionally distributors and online platforms (Art. 8). Compensable damage: death or personal injury, property damage (not exclusively professional property) and corruption of non-professional data (Art. 6). Defectiveness is assessed by the safety the public is entitled to expect (Art. 7). Courts may order disclosure of evidence and presume defectiveness or causation (Arts 9-10). Defences are in Art. 11; liability is joint and several (Art. 12) and cannot be contractually excluded (Art. 15). Limitation period is three years; expiry period is 10 years, or 25 years for latent personal injury (Arts 16-17). Member States may keep or adopt development-risk derogations after notifying the Commission (Art. 18). Final judgments must be published and the Commission sets up a database (Art. 19). Member States transpose by 9 December 2026; rules apply to products placed on the market or put into service after that date (Arts 2, 22).

‘product’ means all movables, even if integrated into, or inter-connected with, another movable or an immovable
‘digital manufacturing file’ means a digital version of, or digital template for, a movable
‘related service’ means a digital service that is integrated into, or inter-connected with, a product
‘component’ means any item, whether tangible or intangible, raw material or related service
‘data’ means data as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2022/868
‘manufacturer’s control’ means that:
‘making available on the market’ means any supply of a product for distribution, consumption or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity
‘placing on the market’ means the first making available of a product on the Union market
‘putting into service’ means the first use of a product in the Union in the course of a commercial activity
‘manufacturer’ means any natural or legal person who:
‘authorised representative’ means any natural or legal person established within the Union who has received a written mandate from a manufacturer
‘importer’ means any natural or legal person who places a product from a third country on the Union market
‘fulfilment service provider’ means any natural or legal person offering, in the course of a commercial activity, at least two of the following services
‘distributor’ means any natural or legal person in the supply chain who makes a product available on the market
‘economic operator’ means a manufacturer of a product or component
‘online platform’ means online platform as defined in Article 3, point (i), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
‘trade secret’ means trade secret as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Directive (EU) 2016/943
‘substantial modification’ means a modification of a product after it has been placed on the market or put into service
any natural person who suffers damage caused by a defective product (the ‘injured person’)
A product shall be considered defective where it does not provide the safety that a person is entitled to expect or that is required under Union or national law.

obligations.summary: In Member State court proceedings for product damage, the defendant is required, on a reasoned request and after the claimant presents sufficient facts and evidence, to disclose relevant evidence at its disposal; disclosure must be limited to what is necessary and proportionate. Member States must ensure this (Art. 9(1) to (3)).

enforcement.note: The directive sets civil liability for compensation of injured natural persons (Arts 5, 8, 12, 16, 17) and contains no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking, and no penalty clause requiring Member States to lay down sanctions. Liability rules are recorded under obligations and related sections, not as enforcement.
